title: Pilau Rice
subtitle: Yellow, cardamom-scented long-grain rice
excerpt: Basmati rice cooked with whole spices and a little turmeric until each grain is separate and fragrant. The proper accompaniment to a curry rather than plain boiled rice.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pilau (also pilaf, pulao, polo) is a method of cooking rice in seasoned broth that spans Persian, Indian, Central Asian, and Turkish cooking. The British curry-house pilau typically uses whole spices fried in butter or ghee, basmati rice, and turmeric for colour.

recipeTools.notes: With a tight-fitting lid for steaming the rice.

content.text: Pilau rice starts with whole spices fried briefly in butter until they release their fragrance, then the washed rice is added with water and turmeric. The key is the ratio: 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water, a tight lid, and no lifting until the steam has done its work. The result is separate, fragrant grains with a light golden colour.

items.preparation: rinsed until water runs clear, soaked 20 minutes

content.text: Rinse the basmati in cold water several times until the water runs clear. Cover with cold water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain well.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid over medium heat. Add the cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaves. Fry for 1 minute until you can smell the spices opening.
Add the drained rice and stir gently to coat in the spiced butter for 1 minute. Add 450 ml cold water, the turmeric, and the salt. Stir once.
Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to the lowest heat and cover with the lid. Cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from the heat and leave to steam, covered, for 5 minutes. Uncover, fluff gently with a fork, and serve. Remove the whole spices as you find them, nobody wants to bite into a clove.
